indicators.label: Alcohol consumption per capita
indicators.source: AIHW Alcohol and Other Drug Treatment Services
indicators.description: Pure alcohol consumed per person aged 15 and over per year. One of the few health indicators showing a sustained positive trend — Australians are drinking significantly less than a generation ago.

indicators.label: Antidepressant prescriptions
indicators.description: Antidepressant prescriptions per 1,000 population dispensed under the PBS. Has tripled since 2000 — Australia is now among the highest prescribers in the OECD.

indicators.label: ASX 200
indicators.description: The S&P/ASX 200 index — tracks the performance of the 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange by market capitalisation.

indicators.label: Autism diagnosis rate
indicators.source: AIHW / ABS Survey of Disability Ageing and Carers
indicators.description: Australians with an autism spectrum disorder diagnosis per 100,000 population. Has risen approximately 4-fold since 2009 — from around 75 to over 260 per 100,000.

indicators.label: Cancer incidence rate
indicators.source: AIHW Australian Cancer Incidence and Mortality
indicators.description: Age-standardised incidence rate of all cancers combined per 100,000 population. Despite an ageing population, the overall rate has been stable or declining slightly since 2000.

indicators.label: Cash rate
indicators.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia's official cash rate target — the interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans, which flows through to mortgages, savings accounts and the broader economy.

indicators.label: CO₂ emissions (Mt)
indicators.description: Australia's total net greenhouse gas emissions in megatonnes of CO₂ equivalent per year, covering all sectors including energy, agriculture, transport and land use.

indicators.label: CPI
indicators.description: Consumer Price Index — measures the change in prices paid by Australian households for a fixed basket of goods and services. The RBA targets 2–3% annual CPI growth.

indicators.label: Electricity price (c/kWh)
indicators.description: Average retail electricity price in cents per kilowatt-hour for Australian households. One of the most directly felt cost-of-living indicators.

indicators.label: GDP per capita
indicators.description: Gross Domestic Product divided by population — the most commonly used measure of average living standards and economic output per person.

indicators.label: Gini coefficient
indicators.description: A measure of income inequality within Australia. Ranges from 0 (perfect equality — everyone earns the same) to 1 (maximum inequality — one person earns everything). Australia's Gini is typically around 0.32–0.34.

indicators.label: Gold spot price (AUD)
indicators.description: Gold spot price in Australian dollars per troy ounce. Gold is widely regarded as a store of value and a safe-haven asset during times of economic or geopolitical uncertainty.

indicators.label: Gross government debt ($bn)
indicators.description: Total face value of Australian Federal Government debt on issue in billions of dollars. Unlike net debt, this does not subtract government financial assets held against the borrowings.

indicators.label: Homelessness (per 100k)
indicators.description: Number of people experiencing homelessness per 100,000 population, as measured by the ABS Census. Includes rough sleepers, people in temporary accommodation, and those in severely overcrowded dwellings.

indicators.label: Household debt to income
indicators.description: Total household debt (mortgages, personal loans, credit cards) as a percentage of annual household disposable income. Australia is consistently among the world's highest.

indicators.label: Housing approvals
indicators.description: Monthly number of new residential dwelling building approvals issued by local councils — a leading indicator of future housing supply.

indicators.label: Life expectancy
indicators.description: Life expectancy at birth, total persons — the average number of years a newborn would live if current mortality rates applied throughout their life.

indicators.label: M2 money supply
indicators.description: Broad money supply (M3) — the total amount of money in the Australian economy, including physical currency, bank deposits, and other liquid assets. Measured in billions of dollars.

indicators.label: Median age
indicators.description: The median age of the Australian population — half the population is older than this, half is younger. A rising median age signals an ageing population.

indicators.label: Median house price
indicators.description: Median residential property price across Australia's 8 capital cities, weighted average. Half of properties sell above this price, half below.

indicators.label: Median worker tax burden
indicators.description: Estimated total government tax burden on a median full-time worker as a percentage of gross wage — combining federal income tax, Medicare levy, GST and an allocation of state/local taxes and levies.

indicators.label: Average weekly earnings
indicators.description: Average weekly ordinary time earnings for full-time adult employees in nominal dollars. Shows absolute pay levels but does not account for inflation — compare with CPI to see real purchasing power changes.

indicators.label: Mental health hospitalisations
indicators.source: AIHW Mental Health Services in Australia
indicators.description: Mental health-related hospital admissions per 100,000 population where the principal diagnosis is a mental health condition.

indicators.label: Net government debt % GDP
indicators.description: Australian Federal Government net debt as a percentage of GDP. Net debt = gross debt minus financial assets held by government (cash, investments). Expressed as % of GDP for comparability across time.

indicators.label: Net overseas migration
indicators.description: Net overseas migration — the number of people arriving in Australia to stay 12+ months, minus those leaving. Includes skilled migrants, international students, working holiday makers and humanitarian entrants.

indicators.label: Obesity rate
indicators.description: Percentage of Australian adults (18+) classified as obese (BMI 30 or above). Age-standardised.

indicators.label: Total population
indicators.description: Estimated Resident Population of Australia — the total number of people living in Australia at a given time, including citizens, permanent residents and long-term visitors.

indicators.label: House price-to-income ratio
indicators.description: Median house price divided by median annual household income — how many years of income it takes to buy a typical home. A ratio of 3x was historically considered affordable; above 5x is severely unaffordable.

indicators.label: Prison population (per 100k)
indicators.description: Number of prisoners per 100,000 adult population. Includes sentenced prisoners and those on remand awaiting trial.

indicators.label: Private credit growth
indicators.description: Annual growth rate of total private sector credit — money borrowed by households and businesses from financial institutions.

indicators.label: Psychological distress rate
indicators.description: Percentage of adults reporting high or very high psychological distress (Kessler K10 score of 22+). Measured in ABS National Health Survey conducted every 3-4 years.

indicators.label: Total public sector employees
indicators.source: ABS 6248.0 Public Sector Employment and Earnings
indicators.description: Total public sector employee jobs across all levels of government — federal (Commonwealth), state/territory, and local government. Includes defence personnel, teachers, nurses, police, public administrators and all other government employees.

indicators.label: Renewable energy %
indicators.description: Renewable energy as a percentage of total electricity generation from the National Electricity Market (NEM). Includes wind, solar (utility and rooftop), hydro and other renewables.

indicators.label: Rental vacancy rate
indicators.description: The percentage of rental properties currently vacant and available for rent. A healthy rental market is typically considered to have a vacancy rate of around 3%.

indicators.label: Suicide rate (per 100k)
indicators.description: Age-standardised suicide rate per 100,000 population. Age-standardisation allows meaningful comparison over time as the population ages.

indicators.label: Tax revenue per capita (real)
indicators.description: Total government tax revenue per person across all levels — federal, state and local — in real (inflation-adjusted) 2022–23 dollars. Shows how much government collects in tax per Australian over time.

indicators.label: Avg temperature anomaly
indicators.description: Annual mean temperature anomaly for Australia relative to the 1961–1990 baseline average. A positive value means that year was warmer than the historical average.

indicators.label: Terms of trade
indicators.description: The ratio of export prices to import prices — how much imports Australia can purchase with a given volume of exports. A rising index means Australia's exports are becoming more valuable relative to what it imports.

indicators.label: Underemployment rate
indicators.description: The percentage of the labour force who are employed but working fewer hours than they want and are available to work more. A more complete measure of labour market slack than unemployment alone.

indicators.label: Unemployment rate
indicators.description: The percentage of the labour force who are unemployed and actively seeking work. Seasonally adjusted.

indicators.label: Wage price index
indicators.description: The Wage Price Index measures changes in the price employers pay for labour, holding quality and quantity of work constant. Base: September 1997 = 100.
